errors.evidence: The legend colors/patterns are misdescribed: + SFT on D₀ is shown in pale yellow with horizontal stripes, and + SFT on D₀, D₁, D₂ is peach/pink with a solid fill, but the description also incorrectly implies the legend/order as a set of SFT conditions without noting the specific visual mapping accurately.

errors.evidence: The y-axis extends to about 85, but the visible labeled tick marks run from 0 to 80 at intervals of 10; 85 is the upper limit, not a tick mark.

errors.text_span: for example, LLaMA-2-7B scores ~67% with no SFT and ~83% with full SFT (D₀–D₂); LLaMA-2-13B improves from ~70% to ~80%; and LLaMA-2-70B rises from ~80% to ~83%.
errors.evidence: These values are approximate and the trend summary overstates some comparisons: for LLaMA-2-13B, the full-SFT value is about 80%, while for LLaMA-2-70B the full-SFT value is about 82–83%; the description also implies monotonic improvement within each model, but the 13B and 70B groups show non-monotonic changes across SFT conditions.

The description does not mention that each model group contains bars with distinct fill patterns (diagonal stripes, horizontal stripes, solid) as a visual encoding detail, nor does it note the legend placement in the bottom-right, both of which are highlighted in the reference.

errors.text_span: The chart visually supports the claim that scaling both model size and SFT dataset leads to better performance on longer math word problems, as reflected in higher CoLeG-R scores.
errors.evidence: This is interpretive language beyond the figure itself. The chart shows values, but it does not directly establish causation about 'leading to better performance' or about solving longer math word problems.
